Wait — which is A and which is B? The user listed C1 as 2023 and C2 as 2022. For chronological order I'd set A = 2022 (C2), B = 2023 (C1). Actually, either way works. Let me pass them clearly labeled in my reply. In fact, the tool doesn't return labels beyond my parameters, but I can describe it myself. To make it natural, I'll go with A = C2 (2022) first, B = C1 (2023).

result.which_side_is_right: not graded: the maps describe different times, so a window where they differ may have changed on the ground, and each map needs a reference of its own date; no labels_date was given, so no grading is possible even with labels
result.evidence_scope: The side-picking evidence (exp58 of 2imi9/olmoearth_inferenceX) was measured on other pairs of maps with labels and does not cover this pair: no recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right, and without labels neither side can be picked.
must_state: No recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right; without labels neither side can be picked.
Maps of different times may differ by real change; labels for one date grade only that date's map; each map needs its own date's reference.
result.where: on map A's predicted-class boundaries more often than windows overall (not whether whole regions flip)
result.boundary_means: boundary_share_overall and boundary_share_of_differing count windows with at least one of their 8 neighbours of a different class in map A's PREDICTED classes: a boundary of map A, not a true class boundary. Every differing window is a change of that whole window's class, on a boundary or not. The shares measure no contiguity: they do not show whether whole regions flip or only their edges.
result.class_pairs_reading: class_pairs counts, for each unordered pair of classes, the windows where one map has one class and the other map the other, both directions together; 'directions' splits that count by which map has which class, as class_changes does.
result.listing_order: the 10 listed windows are the first differing windows in window order (from row 0), not a sample of them; all 3,807 are in the file compare_differing_1cca89d91a.json, in the same order. Read which classes change, in which direction and where from class_changes, class_pairs, spatial and facts, not from the list. review_set_evidence.json (evidence_detail_path) holds evidence text only, no windows

spatial.reading: Each band is a strip of whole rows (row_bands) or whole columns (col_bands) of the window grid, numbered from 0: row band 0 holds row 0, the grid's first rows (the north edge: the scores' window locations put row 0 north), and column band 0 holds column 0. share_of_differing is the band's share of ALL differing windows; share_of_windows is its share of all compared windows, the share an even spread would give it; share_of_band_differing is the share of the band's own windows that differ. top_band_share is row band 0's share_of_differing; max_band is the band, of either axis, holding the most differing windows.

facts.sentence: The most common change is class 2 (shrubland_savanna) in map A to class 4 (grassland_barren) in map B: 1,409 of the 3,807 differing windows (37.0%); the reverse, class 4 (grassland_barren) in map A to class 2 (shrubland_savanna) in map B, is 268 (7.0%).

Map A has the larger margin on 57.8% of the 3,807 differing windows (map B on 42.2%); this does not make A right there: a margin is not a label, and no recorded experiment grades which of these two maps is right.

68.6% of the 3,807 differing windows have a neighbour of another class in map A's predicted classes, against 49.2% of all 16,384 windows; this counts neighbours, not regions, so it does not show whether whole regions flip or only their edges.
Of the 3,807 differing windows, 39.4% lie in the northmost row band (rows 0-31, band 0 of 4), which holds 25.0% of all compared windows; that is the most of any of the 4 row and 4 column bands.

All 3,807 differing windows are listed, in window order, in /Users/lucas/Desktop/Github/olmoearth_inferenceX/exp/out/exp86_trial/rounds/11/runs/B3/cluster/2/workspace/compare_differing_1cca89d91a.json, each with both maps' class and margin.

the maps describe different or overlapping periods (2022-01-01/2022-12-31 and 2023-01-01/2023-12-31): a window where they differ either changed on the ground or is wrong in one map, and another unlabelled map, of any date, cannot tell which; only a reference dated to each map can

no labels were given to this comparison, which takes none: nothing here says which map is right, more accurate or better, and nothing here says whether labels for these maps exist (none was looked up); neither map is shown right where they differ, and the more confident side is not thereby the right one

the maps describe different times (2022-01-01/2022-12-31 and 2023-01-01/2023-12-31): labels or a reference for one date grade only the map of that date, and would count the other wrong wherever the ground changed; one reference plus another model run adds an unlabelled map and settles nothing; to say which map is right where they differ, each map needs a reference of its own date

labels drawn only from the low-confidence, least certain or most ambiguous windows (or from a review set) are not a sample of the map: an error rate over them describes those windows and overstates the map's, so it is no defensible error rate for either map; each of olmoearth_plan_label_sample's designs ('confidence', 'proportional', 'random') draws from every window of the map, and its estimate needs every drawn window labelled

content:
Compared both runs (same model, OlmoEarth-v1-FT-AWF-Base rev a347b15) window-by-window over their shared 128x128 grid (16,384 windows). Map A = C2/2022, Map B = C1/2023.

**Where they differ**
- **3,807 windows differ (23.2%)** of the area.
- Concentrated in the **north**: the top row band (rows 0–31) holds **39.4%** of all differing windows; also skews west (west column band 34.0%).
- Mostly at edges: **68.6%** of differing windows touch a predicted-class boundary in the 2022 map (vs 49.2% of all windows).
- Main class flips (of the 3,807):

| Change (2022 -> 2023) | n | Share |
|---|---|---|
| shrubland_savanna -> grassland_barren | 1,409 | 37.0% |
| woodland_forest -> montane_forest | 447 | 11.7% (one-directional) |
| shrubland_savanna -> woodland_forest | 388 | 10.2% |
| grassland_barren -> urban_dense_development | 336 | 8.8% |
| shrubland_savanna -> urban_dense_development | 308 | 8.1% |

All 3,807 differing windows (with both classes + margins) are saved at `compare_differing_1cca89d91a.json` in the workspace.

**Which is right: cannot be determined from this run**
The two maps describe different years (2022 vs 2023), so every differing window is either real ground change (including seasonal cycles) or an error in one map. No tool output grades either side: the more confident margin belongs to the 2022 map on 57.8% of differing windows vs 42.2% for 2023, but a margin is not a label. Labels for one year would grade only that year's map.

**Next steps (need your input)**
- Give me reference labels for 2022 and for 2023 (a tool can't look these up), and I'll compute per-map accuracy with `olmoearth_classification_metrics`.
- Or I can plan how to spend N labels honestly per map (`olmoearth_plan_label_sample`, then `olmoearth_estimate_map_error`) — say a budget, e.g. 200.
